collection: Concrete Lebesgue and Hausdorff Integral Applications
verification_note: Independent model review and concrete identity checks; no Lean or human peer review claimed.

examples.title: Change the order to create the missing derivative
examples.measure: L^2 on the plane; L^1 on each coordinate
hypotheses: D={0<x<y<1}; F=1_D exp(y^2) is Borel and 0<=F<=e 1_(0,1)^2.
examples.result: Integral over D of exp(y^2) equals (e-1)/2.
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: A measurable region whose entire boundary has positive area
hypotheses: At stage n remove 2^(n-1) middle intervals of length 4^(-n); C is the remaining closed intersection; E=C x [0,1].
examples.result: L^1(C)=1/2; boundary(E)=E; L^2(boundary(E))=1/2; integral_E 2y=1/2; the zero extension is not Riemann integrable.
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: A null measurable set with one nonmeasurable section
examples.measure: Complete L^2 jointly; complete L^1 on sections
hypotheses: V subset [0,1] is non-Lebesgue measurable; E={0} x V. General proof assumes A is Lebesgue measurable in R^(m+n).
examples.result: E is planar measurable and null, but E_0=V is nonmeasurable; arbitrary Lebesgue-measurable sets have measurable sections almost everywhere.
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: Two finite iterated integrals, but no signed Lebesgue integral
examples.measure: L^2 on (0,1)^2; L^1 on each coordinate
hypotheses: f(x,y)=(x^2-y^2)/(x^2+y^2)^2 on (0,1)^2; every one-variable section is continuous and integrable.
examples.result: Integrating y first gives pi/4; integrating x first gives -pi/4; both joint sign parts have infinite integral, so the signed Lebesgue integral is undefined.
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: Two finite iterated sums and no signed double integral
examples.measure: Counting measure on N x N, N={1,2,...}
hypotheses: a(n,m)=1 if m=n, -1 if m=n+1, and 0 otherwise
The product space is sigma-finite; a is measurable
examples.result: Row-first sum 0; column-first sum 1; integral of |a| infinite; signed product integral undefined
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: A logarithm from a positive double integral
examples.measure: Lebesgue measure on (0,infinity) and the finite parameter interval
hypotheses: a>0 and b>0
examples.result: Integral_0^infinity (exp(-a*x)-exp(-b*x))/x dx = log(b/a); derivative with respect to b is 1/b
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: A weighted integral on a parabolic arc
examples.measure: Normalized H^1 restricted to C; L^1 on [0,1]; H^1 agrees with length, H^0 counts points.
hypotheses: gamma(t)=(t,t^2) for 0<=t<=1 is injective and Lipschitz; f(x,y)=x is nonnegative continuous on C.
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: Traversing a circle twice: multiplicity and orientation
examples.measure: Normalized H^1 restricted to the unit circle; L^1 on [0,4pi]; H^0 counts parameter preimages.
hypotheses: gamma(t)=(cos(t),sin(t)) on [0,4pi] is Lipschitz; w(x,y)=x^2 is continuous nonnegative; multiplicity is two except at (1,0), where it is three.
examples.result: Integral_C x^2 dH^1=pi; parameter integral over two traversals=2pi; F=(-y,x) has circulation 4pi over two counterclockwise traversals and 2pi once; outward flux of G=(x,y) is 2pi.
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: Height integral over a paraboloid graph
examples.measure: Normalized H^2 restricted to S; L^2 on the closed unit disk; normalized H^2 equals plane area on 2-planes.
hypotheses: Phi(x,y)=(x,y,x^2+y^2) on the closed unit disk is injective and sqrt(5)-Lipschitz; height h=z is bounded continuous nonnegative on S.
examples.result: Integral_S z dH^2=pi(25 sqrt(5)+1)/60; H^2(S)=pi(5 sqrt(5)-1)/6.
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: A sphere's second moment and a spherical cap
examples.measure: Normalized H^2 restricted to sphere S_R; L^2 on the angular rectangle; H^2 equals surface area.
hypotheses: R>0; spherical map is injective on (0,pi) x (0,2pi), with bounded derivatives; omitted meridian has H^2 measure zero; h=z^2 is continuous and bounded.
examples.result: Integral_(S_R) z^2 dH^2=4pi R^4/3; H^2(S_R)=4pi R^2; cap of height a in [0,2R] has area 2pi R a; outward flux of G(q)=q is 4pi R^3.
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: A fold counts the image twice
examples.measure: L2 on parameter rectangle; normalized H2=L2 on target plane; H0 counting measure
hypotheses: A=[-1,1]x[0,1] is Borel
F(u,v)=(u^2,v) is Lipschitz on A
h(x,y)=x+y is continuous nonnegative on Q
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: Coarea for squared distance, including the critical value
examples.measure: L2 on closed unit disk; normalized H1 arc length on level circles; L1 on target
hypotheses: g(x,y)=x^2+y^2 is smooth and locally Lipschitz
phi:[0,1]->[0,infinity] is Borel
signed extension requires integral_0^1 |phi| finite
examples.result: integral_D phi(g)=pi integral_0^1 phi; integral_D |gradient g|=4pi/3; integral_D |z|^(2a)=pi/(a+1) for a>-1 and infinity for a<=-1
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: A singular map loses all its increase under differentiation
examples.measure: L1=normalized H1 on domain and target lines; H0 counting measure for fibres
hypotheses: C_n are specified absolutely continuous piecewise linear Cantor approximants
C is their continuous monotone uniform limit
C is not Lipschitz or absolutely continuous
undefined derivatives on the null Cantor set are assigned zero only as representatives
examples.result: C'=0 almost everywhere but C(1)-C(0)=1; integral N(C,y)dy=1; q_n=(3/2)^n 1_Kn tends to zero almost everywhere with integral 1 and fails domination and uniform integrability
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: Lost integral mass: concentration, escape, and dilution
examples.measure: Lebesgue measure on (0,1) or R as specified
hypotheses: h_n=1_(n,n+1) on R
Sufficient convergence conditions distinguish finite measure from infinite measure
examples.result: All three sequences tend pointwise to 0 with integral 1; their distinct failures of domination, value-tail uniform integrability, or tightness are proved
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: A parameter derivative misses a concentrating boundary layer
examples.result: I(t)=t*arctan(1/t) for t>0; right derivative I at 0 is pi/2; integral of pointwise right derivative is 0
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.

examples.title: An exponential kernel retrieves a boundary value
hypotheses: g:[0,infinity)->R is bounded and Borel measurable
g is right-continuous at 0
For the optional L/n bound, |g(x)-g(0)|<=L*x for every x>=0
examples.result: Integral_0^infinity n*exp(-n*x)*g(x) dx tends to g(0); error <= L/n under the stated global Lipschitz-at-zero bound
examples.measure_normalization: L^n is complete Lebesgue measure; H^0 is counting measure; H^k uses omega_k/2^k times diameter^k and agrees with L^k on k-planes.
